description: Literature, supersonic aviation, animation, games, measurement, early aircraft, Scottish geography, wine country and ancient history drive a broad run of questions that rewards precise recall rather than comfortable familiarity.

s03e01.description: Mr Men characters, football dribbling, the stethoscope, Bambi and the mullet hairstyle all enter the question set. Food eventually supplies white chocolate, ensuring the episode moves effortlessly from medical instruments and deer to confectionery and unfortunate hair.

s03e02.description: England football managers are ordered chronologically, vehicles are compared by wheel count and mistletoe enters the mix before literature takes over with The Count of Monte Cristo. It is a characteristically abrupt journey from touchlines and tyres to Dumas.

s03e03.description: Avengers actors, Yellow Submarine, wok cooking, the iris of the eye and contractual T and Cs all appear in one eclectic ladder. Aviation provides the sleekest subject when Concorde enters the quiz.

s03e04.description: Greeting cards, extra-virgin olive oil, white flags, Tiger Woods and the Changing of the Guard all appear before Disney royalty arrives in the form of Mufasa. The episode moves from ceremony and sport to The Lion King without bothering with transitions.

s03e05.description: Hagrid, Hedwig, Hogwarts and Hufflepuff are alphabetised before questions turn to margarine, ZIP codes, Alice in Wonderland and Bear Grylls. Solitaire joins the mix as another familiar thing rendered oddly serious by four illuminated answer choices.

s03e06.description: Einstein, Mother Teresa, Nelson Mandela and Barack Obama are placed in Nobel chronology before questions move to joysticks, seesaws, IQ and the Venus de Milo. Measurement then gets suspiciously precise with a nearest-whole-inch question.

s03e07.description: National flags and their colours, the lengths of sporting arenas and the phrase ‘variety is the spice of life’ all feature before First World War aviation produces the Sopwith Camel. Geography, idiom and machinery coexist with remarkably little concern for thematic unity.

s03e08.description: Cities are compared by distance from London, British landmarks are arranged north to south, sourdough appears, ninety seconds becomes a calculation and War and Peace enters the ladder. Mathematics and philosophy later bring in Blaise Pascal.

s03e09.description: Steak doneness, smartphones, eating humble pie, William the Conqueror and Guy Fawkes Night all share the episode. Geography supplies a more scenic diversion with the Isle of Skye.

s03e10.description: Prince William’s royal ancestry, Chelsea at old and new Wembley, Viking 1 on Mars, island nations, dog heights and a pride of lions all appear. Wine geography eventually carries the questions to Chile’s Colchagua Valley.

s03e11.description: Tintin’s Snowy, the Khmer language, the Tokyo Olympics and war photographer Don McCullin precede a leap back into antiquity with Alexander the Great. Cartoons, Cambodia, sport, photography and empire make for a properly restless ladder.
